Class GTNetMessageCodeRegistry

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetMessageCodeRegistry
@Component public class GTNetMessageCodeRegistry extends Object
The one authority on the GTNet protocol: one GTNetProtocolDescriptor per message code.

Category, request/response relationship, payload model, form eligibility, retry policy, delete protection and rule eligibility are all answered from here. Nothing else in the system may restate any of them — the frontend receives the descriptor set over the API instead of keeping its own copy, and the repository derives the list of codes that await a reply instead of hardcoding it.

The core codes are registered during construction from CoreProtocolDescriptors. An application adds its own codes at start-up with register(GTNetProtocolDescriptor). GTNetProtocolStartupValidator then checks that the result is complete before the server starts serving.

    • requestCodesRequiringResponse

      public List<Byte> requestCodesRequiringResponse()
      The wire values of all requests that stay open until an answer arrives.

      This replaces the hardcoded three-element list the repository used to carry, which omitted the token refresh and the exchange sync — so a pending request of either kind never appeared in the pending map the reply gate reads, was not delete-protected, and did not block the deletion of its peer.

      Returns:
      the codes, sorted by value

    • isValidResponse

      public boolean isValidResponse(byte requestCodeValue, byte responseCodeValue)
      Whether a response code is a registered valid answer to a request code, compared by wire value.

      This is what separates an answer from a receipt. GT_NET_ACK_S, GT_NET_DEFERRED_S and GT_NET_ERROR_S are outcomes of the transport and are never valid answers to a request, so a sender that records only registered responses keeps a manually approved request open until the real decision arrives.

      Parameters:
      requestCodeValue - the wire value of the request
      responseCodeValue - the wire value of the answer that came back
      Returns:
      true when the answer is a registered valid response for that request
